name: Telmisartan
summary: An ARB with the longest half-life of the class (~24 h), giving smooth, true once-daily blood-pressure coverage; also shown to reduce cardiovascular events in high-risk patients (ONTARGET).
mechanism: Selectively blocks the AT1 angiotensin II receptor, preventing angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction, aldosterone release, and sodium retention.

safety.pregnancy: Contraindicated in second and third trimesters (fetotoxic)
warnings: Hyperkalemia, especially with ACE inhibitors, potassium-sparing diuretics, or potassium supplements
Rise in serum creatinine with renal impairment

indications: Cardiovascular risk reduction (MI, stroke, CV death) in high-risk patients
clinicalPearls: Longest-acting ARB — an excellent choice when 24-hour trough coverage matters.
It is a partial PPAR-gamma agonist with modest metabolic effects, but this is not an FDA-labeled indication.
good: Hypertension needing robust 24-h coverage; CV risk reduction.
bad: Pregnancy, hyperkalemia, or bilateral renal artery stenosis.
